newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: BoE's Davies says no one-off tricks for EMU entry.
newsitem.headline: BoE's Davies says no one-off tricks for EMU entry.

text.p: Bank of England Deputy Governor Howard Davies said countries seeking to become founding members of Europe's single currency would be well advised to avoid one-off accounting tricks to qualify.

Strict criteria contained in the Maastricht Treaty on economic and monetary union are imperfect but are the minimum safe degree of convergence for countries joining EMU, he wrote in a contribution to the World Economic Forum's magazine, Worldlink.
"It is vital therefore that these criteria should be respected and that the scope for political interpretation which the Treaty provides should be kept to an absolute minimum," he said.

"Furthermore, countries should satisfy themselves that their performance is sustainable. If a country can only meet the convergece criteria through one-off measures of creative accounting, the wise course would be to defer entry."

"A failed EMU, where the strains on the system imposed by an attenmpt to lock together non-convergent economies proved too great, would be far worse for the long-run construction of the EU than no EMU at all," he added.

Countries seeking to join the single currency must meet the criteria this year in order to join EMU in 1999. Britain has not commited itself to joining the project and Prime Minister John Major's cabinet has voiced doubt it will start on time.
